numerical_contract: Actual-column amax, pow2 scales, E4M3 RN, FP32 GEMM accumulation, BF16 dW. Preserve FP8 AB/Z cache boundaries. One column conversion per block, reused globally. Fixed224/56 math/control registers.

candidates.subgroup: Uniform participation mask across active warp lanes; width4 shuffles and two xor/max steps preserve each row's four-lane group.
candidates.decode: Packed E4M3-to-FP16 decode plus exact integer exponent adjustment into BF16 for safe normal pow2 ranges; original floating fallback for exceptional values/ranges. Applied to row-col and cached-Z decode.
candidates.swiglu: Parallelize the three independent column-amax planes over192threads instead of64threads processing all three serially.
candidates.dw_order: One shared stable descending-row-count expert order per CTA, filled by the producer warp before dW tasks. Keep each task's original K accumulation order. Fallback for more than256ownedexperts.
candidates.dw_pipeline: Three operand stages. Reuse dead activation-conversion scratch space for the dW arena, preventing an unnecessary shared-memory sum of nonoverlapping lifetimes.
candidates.dw_scale: Load per-column scales before WGMMA issue, keeping them in registers through promotion; measure added spill against potential latency hiding.
candidates.pull3: Use the otherwise idle third control warp for row pulls, keeping224/56register partition.
candidates.pull_direct: Warp-vector global loads/stores of already-quantized source packets, avoiding per-row shared-buffer TMA roundtrip. Keep row publication fences.
candidates.swi_packed: Use three hardware BF16x2 rounding operations instead of six scalar bit-rounding sequences in each FP8 SwiGLU pair; preserve nonfinite scalar behavior via fallback and preserve dprob FMA order.
candidates.dw_joint: Stable descending-row-count order with both dW1/dW2 tile sets together for each expert, rather than restarting the expert order in separate dW2 then dW1 queue halves.
candidates.fwd_pack: Round FC1 accumulators to the existing BF16 boundary once, pack pairs, and compute packed integer amax before the unchanged AB quantization/SwiGLU path. Intended to shorten the FP32 live range.

procedure: Build immutable independent source snapshots; finish all compilation before GPU measurements. Validate candidates with full EP8 parity/protocol checks on all3modeldimensions. Screen identical workloads including bracketed FP8 baseline and BF16; then combine and repeat long unprofiled tests for winners. Do not sum FWD/BWD host API timers as GPU kernel timings.

limitations: Single-node EP8 only; no multi-node performance claim.
Unprofiled wall measurements and profiler GPU kernel durations remain separate.
Performance ratios compare matching input/routing hashes within a run; different sample counts use different workload traces.
Compiler spill byte counts are static, not dynamic traffic.
Correctness tests use 257 tokens with tails, empty ranks and protocol stress; no training convergence claim.
Most parity checks use 16 global experts; combined Qwen35B uses 256. Performance uses the full model expert counts.

decision.reason: Retain one universal FC1 reduction/shuffle change: small cycle improvement across six cases, with forward-ready improvements onQ122/Flash and effectively flatQ35. No model-specific tuning.
limitations: Cycle gains are small, about0.2-1.0%; no large-speedup claim.
Q35 FWD wall including release is0.4-0.7%slower against bracket means; checkpoint-ready is effectively flat and20Kbaseline drifts2.3%. Both scopes retained.
Q35 still does not beat BF16.
Static SASS REDUX.MAX drops12to0, but MATCH.ANY and WARPSYNC counts increase. Dynamic instruction reduction has not been established.

rejection_reasons.decode: Exact unit tests pass, but screen latency increases6.9-12.5%.
rejection_reasons.swiglu: Parallel amax has mixed results (-1.4 to+2.6% latency).
rejection_reasons.dw_order: Screen wins onQwen fail to generalize toFlash; combined confirmation is mixed.
rejection_reasons.dw_pipeline: Three stages and scratch reuse fit shared memory, but no consistent performance gain.
rejection_reasons.pull3: Extra pull warp has mixed results; no stable win.
rejection_reasons.pull_direct: Direct vector copies regress up to19.1% in screen.
rejection_reasons.swi_packed: Bitwise tests pass; packed combination is flat/slower in30sample confirmation.
rejection_reasons.dw_joint: Combined expert-major dW1/dW2 scheduling helpsQ122slightly but regressesFlash.
rejection_reasons.fwd_pack: No spill reduction; final cycle has mixed results includingFlash8Kregression.

notes: The full EP8 subgroup checks on all3models ran against this same FC1 source; no candidate kernel changes were made after validation.
Fixed224/56 tile.cuh change predates this experiment and is preserved.

sass-comparison.note: Static SASS counts for the Qwen35B FP8 local FWD entry, not dynamic instruction counts or direct timing attribution.

Compile decode_check.cu and tests/cuda/fp8_column.cu with -O2 -std=c++17 -arch=sm_90a and -Ibuild/fp8-profile-opt/trees/decode/src -Iinclude -I/opt/cutlass/include; output binaries in build/fp8-profile-opt.
python benchmarks/experiments/fp8_profile_opt/evaluate.py subgroup decode swiglu dw_order dw_pipeline dw_scale pull3 pull_direct

Use combine.py label [selected variants] and build_isolated.py label for combinations. Keep each comparison on identical workload and fixed224/56. Build packed and combined, compile swiglu_check.cu against trees/packed/src with the flags above, then run followup.py. Build and check fwd_pack, then run benchmark.py --native-root build/fp8-profile-opt --labels baseline subgroup fwd_pack bf16 baseline_after --mode cycle --warmups 10 --samples 30 --output build/fp8-profile-opt/final-cycle.
benchmark.py supports cycle/forward/backward; use --warmups 10 --samples 30 for confirmation and preserve raw outputs in new directories.
